page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It runs on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores clocked at 3.5 GHz. The CPU provides 54 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware instructions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 16 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. In addition, the instance integrates 237 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable single-threaded capability accompanied by moderate multi-core throughput commensurate with a four-thread configuration. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution reached 1892.08 points in the average range, while multi-core operations scored 3862.58 in the bottom quartile. Geekbench returned 1601.0 points for single-core tasks and 3388.0 points for multi-core processing, displaying average performance in text manipulation alongside lower throughput in code compilation and image processing. PassMark CPU testing yielded 5883.55 points, while memory subsystem evaluation showed 1932.44 points with 30.03 GB/s large-block read bandwidth.

The inclusion of direct-attached NVMe storage and dedicated network capacity provides balanced I/O efficiency without requiring external EBS configuration for temporary scratch spaces. However, the modest vCPU count limits horizontal scaling and compute-heavy throughput. Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is primarily suited for general-purpose application hosting, low-to-moderate throughput web serving, distributed caching nodes, continuous integration workers, and relational database systems that benefit from low-latency local NVMe scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16 GB of DDR4 system memory, and a 237 GB local NVMe SSD, this server balances general-purpose computation with high-speed local storage access. Networking performance offers a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, while vector processing is aided by AVX-512 extensions. Benchmark results show average single-threaded execution alongside constrained multi-threaded scaling due to the four-vCPU hardware footprint. Memory bandwidth registers at 30.03 GB/s on large un-cached reads, and Redis operations achieve 3.96 million operations per second. The m6idn.xlarge is well aligned for mid-tier web serving, intermediate database hosting, caching layers, and applications requiring low-latency temporary storage.
